title: Rocket Boys
author: Homer Hickam Jr.
edition_analyzed: Standard U.S. edition (1998) by Delacorte Press
target_audience: Teens and adults interested in space, rocketry, or STEM
Readers of American memoir and coming-of-age stories
Educators seeking inspiring science and history narratives
General audiences interested in mid-century American life
core_themes: Perseverance and ambition in the face of adversity
The value of education and scientific inquiry
Community—both its support and its constraints
primary_purpose: To chronicle the true story of Homer Hickam’s teenage years in Coalwood, West Virginia, focusing on his quest—along with his friends—to build rockets and escape the limitations of a declining coal-mining town.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person memoir; vivid, reflective, and often humorous
structure_format.organization: Chronological chapters tracing high school years, major rocket launches, and personal milestones
features: Rich depictions of Appalachian small-town life
Interludes on family and local history

key_concepts_lessons: Resourcefulness and teamwork can overcome a lack of resources.
Mentors and teachers significantly shape young lives.
Science and education open pathways beyond difficult circumstances.
Parental support may be indirect or difficult to understand, but it often exists.
Dreams may clash with tradition and expectation but are worth pursuing.
Failure is an inevitable step on the path to success.
notable_features: Eyes-on-the-ground view of America's mid-20th-century coal towns
Technical yet accessible accounts of amateur rocketry
Award-winning memoir adapted as the film ‘October Sky’
Strong characterization of Hickam’s friends, family, and teachers
cultural_historical_context: Set in the 1950s in Coalwood, West Virginia, during the space race and the decline of the American coal industry, capturing both Cold War anxieties and small-town American values.
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed; finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award
Frequently included in high school and college curricula
Inspired a generation of young readers interested in STEM
Adapted into the successful film ‘October Sky’
Lauded for its inspirational message and vivid sense of time and place
comparable_titles: Hidden Figures by Margot Lee Shetterly
The Glass Castle by Jeannette Walls
A Prayer for Owen Meany by John Irving (novel, for similar coming-of-age themes)
October Sky (film adaptation of this book)
